newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-UNIBANKA MERGER ONLY ON COMMERCIAL BASIS-BANKERS.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-UNIBANKA MERGER ONLY ON COMMERCIAL BASIS-BANKERS.

text.p: Foreign shareholders of Unibanka believe any merger with Zemes Banka must be on commercial grounds and that earlier merger plans were becoming politically driven, international bankers and investors said on Thursday.
"The external shareholders feel that they cannot support the merger as originally planned," one banker told Reuters.
The main foreign institutions which have invested into Unibanka are the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and Swedfund.
A planned merger of Unibanka and Zemes was cancelled unexpectedly last month, with both banks saying that the synergies of the deal were not as great as at first thought.

The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA), which controls the government's 33 percent stake in Unibanka, was unhappy as it was not informed of the ending of the merger and has said it believes it should still go ahead.
The international banker said it had become apparent to the shareholders that the merger was politically rather than commercially driven but would not elaborate on what this meant.
The banker said that any merger should take place on purely commercial grounds only.
Unibanka earlier announced that an extraordinary shareholder meeting to discuss the merger has been postponed to June 2 from April 21 to allow the EBRD and the LPA to coordinate their views.
